title: South Africa's ANC Suffers Its Worst Election Result Ever
summary:
South Africa's governing party, the ANC, has just had its worst election result ever. Voters delivered the verdict in local elections held across the country, and even the party itself called the outcome 'catastrophic.'

The ANC is the party that led South Africa out of apartheid, the old system that separated people by race, and into democracy more than 30 years ago under Nelson Mandela. Since then it has won almost every election. Not this time.

The party won a majority in just one of the country's nine provinces, Limpopo. In 2021 it won six. It also won the most votes in only two of the eight big cities, down from six.

The Democratic Alliance came second overall with 25% of the vote and kept control of Cape Town. Former president Jacob Zuma's MK party came third with 10% and took the city of Durban. The Economic Freedom Fighters came fourth with 6%.

'This has been a very catastrophic outcome for the ANC,' said the party's secretary-general, Fikile Mbalula. He blamed the high cost of living, saying middle-class voters had turned against the party in big numbers.

President Cyril Ramaphosa, who leads both the country and the ANC, said the party accepts the result. 'We accept the will of the people,' he said, 'with humility. It is a decline that is concerning.'

The result continues a slide that began in 2024, when the ANC lost its majority in the national parliament for the first time since 1994 and had to share power in a coalition government. Analyst Susan Booysen said the message from voters was devastating, and pointed to poor services as the main reason: problems with water, power and sanitation 'have really been affecting the lives of ordinary people.'

Another analyst, William Gumede, called it 'the end of the liberation movement era in South Africa.' He said the ANC could be the second-biggest party by 2029, and noted that voting is becoming less divided by race. Now the parties have 14 days to negotiate coalitions to run towns and cities, and the ANC could even be shut out of Johannesburg and Pretoria.
why_it_matters: Elections are how people in a democracy tell their leaders what they think, and this result shows voters punishing a party they feel has let them down on everyday services like water and power.
